statement: A did:dht suffix is the z-base-32 encoding of the Ed25519 identity public key; the identity verification method takes fragment `0` while its JWK `kid` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint, never `0`.

A DID DHT v0 document maps to an authoritative DNS response packet with ID 0, TTL 7200, and compressed names; root, verification-method, relationship, service, alsoKnownAs, controller, and type-index records follow the v0 property mapping, omitting defaults only where decoding restores them.
DNS TXT character strings hold at most 255 bytes; longer logical values span segments without splitting UTF-8 code points, and authoritative-gateway NS records carry fully qualified domain names.
BEP44 messages sign the exact preimage `3:seqi<seq>e1:v<len>:<value>` over the raw compressed DNS bytes with a monotonically increasing integer sequence, and the value is at most 1000 bytes.

Pkarr relay PUT bodies are `signature[64] || sequence_be[8] || v` with content type application/octet-stream addressed at the gateway identity URL; a terminal non-2xx rejects the publication and never reports success.

Current Enbox agent documents use verification methods `#0` (identity; authentication, assertion, invocation, delegation), `#sig` (authentication, assertion), `#enc` (key agreement), and an optional `#dwn` DecentralizedWebNode service; decoding normalizes method type to JsonWebKey, fills default algorithms and thumbprint kids, and coerces endpoints to arrays.
Codec round trips preserve the decoder fixpoint: for every supported decoder output, decode(encode(decode(x))) equals decode(x).
Current TypeScript Enbox enforces the 1000-byte BEP44 limit on the signing preimage instead of the value; corrections check `v` alone.
Current TypeScript Enbox splits TXT values at UTF-16 code-unit boundaries instead of UTF-8 byte boundaries.
Current TypeScript Enbox parses TXT properties by splitting on every `=`, truncating values that contain it.
Current TypeScript Enbox emits the full gateway URI, not its host, as NS record data.
